full_judgment:
KM Hasan J: The accused petitioner seeks leave to appeal against three judgments and orders dated 8-8-2001 passed by a Division Bench of the high Court Division discharging the Rules in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 7753, 7754 and 7755 of 2000. The leave applications are disposed of by this judgment as the facts and law points involved are similar. 

 2. Complainant respondent Nos. 2 in the three applications are three different persons who Ii led separate complaint petitions against the accused in the court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate being petition case Nos. 1812, 1811 and 2901 of 1999 under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The learned Metropolitan Magistrate took cognizance against the petitioner in all the cases. 

 3. On 24-6-1999 the accused petitioner filed Title Suit No. 129 of 1999 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka challenging the validity of an agreement and praying for a declaration that the deed of agreement and the memorandum of understanding are void and not binding upon the plaintiff. At the same time the accused petitioner tiled an application under section 344 of the Code of Criminal Procedure tor staying the proceedings of the aforesaid cases Pending before the Metropolitan Magistrate. The learned Magistrate after hearing both the parties stayed the proceedings for a period of six months. The three complainant respondents then filed before the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge criminal revisional applications which were allowed by the learned Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 4th Court. Dhaka and the order of the learned Magistrate staying the proceedings of the cases were set aside. Against that order accused petitioner obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 7753, 7754 and 7755 of 200() which were discharged by the High Court Division on the ground that the civil suit will not he in any way a hindrance to procced in criminal cases since there is no possibility of any conflicting decision in the civil suit and the criminal cases. 

 4. The learned Advocate for accused petitioner submits that the High Court Division has committed an error of law by discharging the Rules. He further submits that where the facts reveal that the transaction in question involves civil liability no criminal proceeding will lie and the criminal cases are liable to be quashed. 

 5. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocate and gone through the judgment and find no substance in the submission of the learned Advocate since under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act an offence is committed if a cheque is dishonoured and if payment is not made within 15 days after receipt of a legal notice. It is a settled law that criminal proceeding can be proceeded independently of the civil suit. Moreover, since there is a prima facie case the criminal cases cannot also be quashed. Therefore, the High Court Division did not commit any illegality or made any error in law by holding that the pendency of the civil suit will not he hindrance to proceed with the criminal cases.
